a: Stoichiometry uses balanced equations to relate amounts of reactants/products.
The limiting reagent is fully consumed and limits product amount.
Coefficients give mole ratios between species in a reaction.
Concentration measures amount of solute per amount of solution.
Solubility is how much solute dissolves under given conditions.
At equilibrium, forward and reverse rates are equal.
Systems at equilibrium shift to counteract imposed changes.
Buffers resist pH changes when small amounts of acid/base are added.
Electrolysis uses electricity to drive non-spontaneous reactions.
Hydrocarbons contain primarily carbon and hydrogen.
